Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `CommandLineTest_testGetOptionValue.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/commons-cli/manual/testcases/CommandLineTest/CommandLineTest_testGetOptionValue.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

I've read both files. The original test has substantial dead code: four unused `@MethodSource` provider methods (`createHasOptionParameters`, `createOptionValuesParameters`, `createParsedOptionValueParameters`, `createParsedOptionValuesParameters`), an unused `assertWritten` helper, and several unused imports — none of which are exercised by the single executing test `testGetOptionValue` (which uses only `createOptionValueParameters`). I'll remove that clutter and clarify the repeated `optValue == null ? "thing" : optValue` ternaries with named locals, without changing any CUT call.Compilation succeeded (`COMPILE_OK`). The refactored test preserves all original `getOptionValue` calls, arguments, and expected outcomes while removing four unused `@MethodSource` providers, the unused `assertWritten` helper, and dead imports, and clarifying the repeated default-value ternaries with named locals (`DEFAULT_TEXT`, `optWithDefault`, `grpWithDefault`) plus section comments.
